candidate.title: MAINE-Seq / MNase-Seq / Nucleo-Seq
candidate.scope: Grouped Illumina poster schematic, middle row only, labeled MAINE-Seq, MNase-Seq and Nucleo-Seq. The active route is Open chromatin → MNase digestion → Isolate trimmed complexes → DNA extraction → DNA. The left yellow-highlighted nucleosome cartoon is a descriptive assay icon without a transfer arrow or keyed modification. The two isolated nucleosome drawings represent one product class; no branching or pooling is shown. Neighboring DNaseI-SIM and FiT-seq rows are outside the assigned target. All three names are retained as targets of this shared schematic, without asserting aliases, identical complete implementations or interchangeability. Operation assignments refer to the poster depiction. For Nucleo-Seq, the primary-supported interpretation explicitly distinguishes the drawn pre-extraction intact-complex isolation from Valouev's post-extraction DNA size selection (correction c_nucleo_selection). Library construction and sequencing are text-supported downstream interfaces, not additional depicted operations.

Mapping fragment-derived reads supports genomic localization and population-level nucleosome occupancy/position patterns; the readout is protection-dependent rather than an unbiased census of all genomic DNA.

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Treat the drawn chromatin with micrococcal nuclease, cleaving exposed DNA and leaving trimmed DNA protected by chromatin proteins available for recovery.
operations.mechanism: MNase is the nuclease reagent, depicted as orange circles at exposed/linker DNA; it is not a second material product or a branch. Bound chromatin proteins protect portions of DNA from digestion.
operations.information_effect: Protection is converted into the surviving genomic DNA fragment population. Nucleosome icons establish the main depicted target; survival alone does not identify every protecting protein or prove perfect nucleosome specificity.

operations.label: DNA extraction
operations.description: Recover DNA from the retained DNA–protein complexes, producing the free DNA fragments drawn at the right endpoint. This local input is s_complex after the depicted isolation. For the Valouev-associated Nucleo-Seq implementation, the paper reports extraction after digestion and selection of purified DNA afterward; that interface is distinguished in c_nucleo_selection rather than substituted into this drawn route.
operations.mechanism: The schematic leaves deproteinization and DNA purification broad.
operations.information_effect: The sequenced carrier is DNA derived from protected chromatin, not histone protein. Subsequent library construction preserves genomic sequence and fragment-origin information for nucleosome mapping. Protein identity and histone modifications are not directly encoded by this route. MNase sequence preference and differential digestion sensitivity can affect which fragments survive; occupancy is not synonymous with accessibility.

method_scopes.rationale: Resolved at the declared grouped-poster scope: operation_ids retains the three local operations that the poster places under Nucleo-Seq. This assignment describes the shared drawing, not verification that all three local material interfaces occur in the poster-associated Valouev implementation. Valouev full text supports MNase digestion of chromatin and sequencing of protected DNA. Its Methods deproteinizes and extracts DNA after digestion, then size-selects purified DNA before library construction. Accordingly, op_isolate (s_digest → intact DNA–protein complexes s_complex) is supported for Nucleo-Seq only as the shared poster depiction; it is not Valouev's documented selection operation. The fixed s_complex input history of the drawn op_extract is also retained as poster depiction and is not assigned to Valouev's direct digest-to-DNA extraction interface. The primary-supported correspondence is recovery of nucleosome-protected DNA, with different selection substrate and order; correction c_nucleo_selection records this resolved interpretation. No primary-specific operation or alternate branch is added to the image graph. Valouev used SOLiD sequencing, so this Illumina catalogue does not establish an Illumina implementation of that paper. The matching collection additionally associates Nucleo-Seq with Chodavarapu (reference 254), whose full text supports an Illumina library from MNase-digested mononucleosome DNA, without verifying the poster's intact-complex isolation step or replacing the literal poster's Valouev association. Nuc-seq and ChEC-seq are catalogue context, not additional assigned targets.

corrections.diagram_observation: The grouped MAINE-Seq / MNase-Seq / Nucleo-Seq poster row places Isolate trimmed complexes (op_isolate) after MNase digestion and before DNA extraction. Its output s_complex is visibly DNA still associated with nucleosomal proteins, and that isolated-complex state is the fixed input of the following op_extract.
corrections.primary_statement: The literal poster reference assigns Valouev et al. (2011) to Nucleo-Seq. In full-text Methods [b00015], after MNase digestion the material is deproteinized and DNA is extracted; the paper then size-selects purified DNA to obtain mononucleosome-core DNA for library construction. Thus the documented selection acts on extracted DNA after protein removal, rather than on intact DNA–protein complexes before extraction. The Nucleo-Seq scope adopts this primary-supported interpretation: the paper supports MNase-protected DNA recovery and sequencing, but does not establish the drawn op_isolate or the subsequent op_extract input history as local Valouev operations. Those operation IDs remain assigned solely at the shared poster-depiction scope, and the source graph is preserved. Only a purpose correspondence between recovering nucleosome-protected DNA and the poster recovery block is supported; their substrates and order are not equated.
